changelog.change: Seed rule set to API level 35. The policy scraper must update this value when Google Play raises the requirement.
Repointed. The rule cited "Target API level requirements for Google Play apps", which is the page name, not a heading on it. A person chose the real top heading of the same document.

Gated on submitting_to_store. The rule fired on 41 of 346 published apps, and every one of them is listed on Google Play today. The floor blocks a submission, not a listing, so an error on a shipped app was a false positive.

description: Google Play blocks a submission and an update whose target API level is below the current requirement. It does not remove an app already listed, so this applies to a build you are about to upload and not to one that already ships. The requirement rises every year, so this rule holds a version number that the rule pipeline must keep current.

remediation.summary: Raise targetSdk to the level that Google Play requires, then test the behavior changes that the new level introduces.

Verification graded this rule understated and named no fix that a pass can apply. A person must read it. Split the rule into separate checks based on app_type (new vs existing) and platform (Wear OS/Automotive/TV/XR/standard), each requiring the correct minimum API level (36 for new standard apps, 35 for existing apps, 35 for new Wear OS/Automotive, 34 for new TV/XR), rather than a single flat minimum of 35.

Promoted. Verification graded it accurate. The corpus never ran it, because a precondition needs a fact no published app declares, so this grade is the only evidence behind it.

description: The app's targetSdkVersion must meet Google Play's minimum required API level, which depends on app type and submission date. New apps/updates generally need API 36+, with exceptions for Wear OS/Automotive (35+) and TV/XR (34+). Existing apps need at least API 35 to remain available to new users on newer Android versions. The floor here is the one for an existing app. A new standard app needs 36, and a new TV or XR app needs 34. Nothing in a repository says which of those an app is, so this check reads the level that holds for every existing app and reports no app wrongly.

interpretations.interpretation: Checker enforces the general-purpose app minimum (API 35) as a baseline; exact required level varies by app category (Wear OS, TV, Automotive, XR) and by submission date, which a mechanical check cannot fully resolve.
The rule could instead require API 36 for new apps depending on submission timing relative to August 31 2026 deadline.

remediation.summary: Update the app's targetSdkVersion in build.gradle to at least API level 35 (or higher per app type/date requirements) before uploading to Google Play.
